text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Ten Danish businesses are attempting to get leading debit card Dankort linked to the internet.

--Leading institutional investors are demanding that chemical manufacturer Cheminova explain how it will ensure that its products are safely used, after a critical TV documentary on the use of pesticides sold abroad but banned at home.
--Telecoms company Sonofon says that it is considering leasing state railway DSB's fibre-optic cables.
--The Danish bankers' association says that tough competition and the small margin between deposit and loan interest rates will neccesitate more incentives to customers.
--The Confederation of Danish Industries says that there appeared to be an upturn at the beginning of 1997 but growth in manufacturing industry still looks slower than in other business areas.
--April 1997 new car sales were up 1.5 percent on the same month last year, to 14,777.
--Novo Nordisk's first quarter results showed a one percent year-on-year rise in profits before and after tax, an eight percent rise in the operating result and a seven percent rise in sales.
--Cheminova downgraded its 1997 pre-tax profits forecast to unchanged from 1996 from a previous prediction of a 10 percent rise.
-- Social Affairs Minister Karen Jespersen intends to give the unemployed with capital savings six months of benefit before they are obliged to start drawing on their savings.
